learning_phases.title: Get the source and identify the main folders
learning_phases.goal: Create a dedicated upstream-derived checkout and record its source revision without changing flight behavior.
learning_phases.concept: Source code, a checkout, a commit and a built executable are different things.
read_focus: Project README and direction; upstream source-download guide.
Selected checkout: ardupilot — ArduCopter/, libraries/, Tools/, waf and pinned submodules.
learning_phases.change_scope: Source acquisition and local version/origin notes only; no firmware edits or simulator installation.
steps: Choose a dedicated checkout location and inspect existing paths before creating it.
Clone the official source, select and record a base revision and matching submodules.
Walk through the three main folders and explain where vehicle logic, reusable libraries and developer tools live.
success: Origin, exact commit and submodule revisions are recorded.
The user can point to vehicle code versus shared libraries; no build/flight success is inferred.
evidence: Checkout path, credential-free origin, commit and submodule listing.
A short folder map and untouched-baseline status.
learning_phases.rollback: Keep the acquired source separate; revert only task-owned notes/checkout changes if needed and preserve unrelated paths.
learning_phases.teach_back: Which folder contains Copter-specific behavior, and which contains reused controllers?
learning_phases.record: 2026-10-31: source acquisition and guided orientation complete. Copter-4.7.2 at fb773567896014da007bca58358704d4a0d8516f; main worktree and all 21 recursive submodules clean and matching parent pins. Source only, not build/flight qualified. Learner identified ArduCopter/; shared-controller location clarified. [Execution record](../../evidence/l01-source-and-orientation/README.md), [revision manifest](../../evidence/l01-source-and-orientation/source-baseline.json) and [Git output](../../evidence/l01-source-and-orientation/git-evidence.txt). L02 remains planned; P01 remains in_progress. Follow-up location correction: visible `ardupilot/` development checkout on local branch `featherlane/dev`, with the source pin and all submodules unchanged.

learning_phases.title: Build and launch basic SITL
learning_phases.goal: Run one unchanged ArduCopter SITL instance on the selected environment while disarmed.
learning_phases.concept: SITL is the autopilot executable plus simulated sensors/physics; a 3D world can come later.
read_focus: Official macOS build setup and the selected source revision's prerequisite/build scripts.
Tools/autotest/sim_vehicle.py and the actual build output/startup log.
learning_phases.change_scope: Machine/toolchain qualification, scoped dependencies and a reproducible basic SITL launch; no Gazebo, ROS, AI or product UI.
steps: Record actual Mac architecture/OS and inspect required tools and any prerequisite script before using it.
Qualify the unchanged build and launch one standard vehicle with the minimum useful ground-console view.
Read heartbeat/mode/readiness, then stop only owned processes and repeat the launch.
success: One disarmed instance starts, reports usable state and shuts down cleanly.
Actual versions, endpoint and repeatable commands are recorded. A platform blocker is recorded as blocked, not complete.
evidence: Mac/toolchain version tuple, source pin, start/stop commands and startup log.
Any native-Mac limitation and a bounded fallback decision.
learning_phases.rollback: Stop owned simulator processes and return to the recorded baseline; document installed dependencies and preserve user configuration.
learning_phases.teach_back: Which process runs ArduPilot, and where do its sensor measurements come from?
learning_phases.record: 2026-10-31: unchanged Copter-4.7.2 built on macOS 15.7.7 arm64 / Apple Clang 17 / Python 3.12.12. Two sequential fresh stock quad SITL launches reported disarmed STABILIZE, simulated GPS and EKF3 GPS use; owned processes stopped and sockets cleared after each. [Execution/runbook](../../evidence/l02-basic-sitl-setup/README.md), [environment/source tuple](../../evidence/l02-basic-sitl-setup/environment.json) and [actual run results](../../evidence/l02-basic-sitl-setup/run-results.json). Startup dependency failure, four MAVProxy parsing errors per run and terrain limitations retained. Learning checkpoint completed in this chat on 2026-10-31: learner explained compilation, SITL and the ground console; follow-up clarified SITL as the simulation setup and successful launch versus successful flight. No arming/flight or custom firmware. L03 remains planned; P01 remains in_progress.

learning_phases.title: Watch one takeoff hold and landing
learning_phases.goal: Perform one simple stock simulated flight through the existing console.
learning_phases.concept: A requested command, an acknowledgment and achieved movement are separate events.
read_focus: Selected stock mode and console commands qualified for this build.
Telemetry/log fields for mode, altitude, vertical speed, landed state and arming.
learning_phases.change_scope: No custom flight code. Use the unchanged vehicle and a clear basic scene.
steps: Explain the expected takeoff, hold, land and disarm sequence before running it.
Issue each supported action and observe its resulting state.
Save a short command/state timeline and cleanly end the session.
success: Takeoff, a controlled hold, landing and disarm are observed and recorded.
Rejected/unready states are explained rather than hidden by a success label.
evidence: Command/state timeline and the retained simulator/flight log.
Observed limitations and one sentence explaining the result.
learning_phases.rollback: Use the qualified simulator stop/terminal procedure and restore its baseline configuration.
learning_phases.teach_back: What evidence tells us that takeoff actually happened rather than merely being accepted?
learning_phases.record: [Observed stock flight](../../evidence/l03-first-stock-flight/README.md): takeoff to 3 m, declared 5-second hold, LAND and automatic disarm; clean shutdown. Guided learner checkpoint completed in this chat on 2026-10-31: learner identified observed telemetry, height near 3 m and vertical speed as evidence of takeoff/hold/landing; follow-up clarified flight state and automatic disarm. This is a guided checkpoint, not independent verification.

learning_phases.title: Trace one flight command through the code
learning_phases.goal: Follow one observed command from its receiver or active mode to navigation, control and motor output.
learning_phases.concept: Mission, mode, navigation, feedback control and estimation have distinct jobs.
read_focus: Selected checkout: relevant GCS_MAVLink handler and active mode file.
The calls actually used by that mode into AC_WPNav, AC_PosControl, AC_AttitudeControl, AP_Motors and estimator state.
learning_phases.change_scope: Read-only walkthrough and annotations; optional existing debugger/log tools only after checking their effect on timing.
steps: Choose one action from the previous flight and locate its actual receiver/mode path.
Read only the functions needed to connect the action to reference generation and control.
Draw the observed chain in plain language and connect each stage to the saved flight timeline.
success: The user can explain the selected path and identify which part estimates state versus produces motor demand.
Source links/line references match the pinned checkout, rather than older tutorial APIs.
evidence: A short source-linked walkthrough for one command.
A note about any gaps or timing effect of observation tools.
learning_phases.rollback: Remove only optional task-owned debug instrumentation; keep the unchanged baseline available.
learning_phases.teach_back: Where is the destination selected, and where are individual motor outputs calculated?
learning_phases.record: [Pinned-source GUIDED takeoff walkthrough](../../evidence/l04-trace-one-command/README.md): request admission, target, estimator feedback, position/attitude control, motor mixer and simulated outputs traced against the L03 evidence. Guided learner checkpoint completed in this chat on 2026-10-31: learner located read_inertia/AHRS state reads and AP_MotorsMatrix mixing. Follow-up clarified that the estimator supplies current state, controllers consume it, and both estimation and control run inside ArduPilot rather than MAVProxy. This is guided understanding, not an independent examination. No new flight, firmware changes or runtime instrumentation.

learning_phases.title: Fly to one known coordinate
learning_phases.goal: Reach one nearby known destination using a qualified stock AUTO or GUIDED path.
learning_phases.concept: A destination needs a frame, units, origin and altitude reference.
read_focus: The selected stock destination-ingress path and coordinate conversion.
Existing mission/path illustration for frame terminology.
learning_phases.change_scope: One destination via existing console/mission tooling; no custom mission runtime or target detector.
steps: Write down the goal and coordinate/height conventions and predict the movement.
Use one qualified stock execution path in an obstacle-free scene.
Compare requested goal with measured vehicle position and speed.
success: The intended coordinate is reached through the selected stock path.
The origin/sign conventions and actual terminal behavior are documented.
evidence: Goal/frame, parameters and measured trajectory.
Source-linked explanation of destination acceptance.
learning_phases.rollback: Restore the known mission/parameters and use the qualified terminal procedure.
learning_phases.teach_back: What would change if the same numeric coordinate used a different origin or altitude frame?
learning_phases.record: [One stock coordinate flight](../../evidence/l05-one-coordinate/README.md): GUIDED DO_REPOSITION to latitude -35.3632172°, longitude 149.1652374°, 3 m above home; about 5 m north. Accepted request, measured movement, five-second low-speed goal hold, LAND/automatic disarm and clean shutdown observed. Guided height-reference checkpoint complete on 2026-10-31. Startup invalid positions and four parsing errors retained; no speed tuning or firmware edits. One run only; P03 broader gate and P01 failure-handling remain open.

learning_phases.title: Change one speed limit and compare
learning_phases.goal: Repeat the same route with one changed speed setting and explain the difference.
learning_phases.concept: Speed limits influence travel time; acceleration and stopping remain separate constraints.
read_focus: The selected mode's actual speed parameter/API, units and persistence semantics.
Measured position and velocity traces from L05.
learning_phases.change_scope: One qualified speed setting; keep route, controller tuning and scene fixed.
steps: Record the original setting and predict the visible effect of the change.
Repeat the identical route with the single change.
Compare actual speed/travel/stop behavior, then restore or explicitly retain the chosen setting.
success: The changed setting and observed effect are clear, including any difference from the prediction.
No unexplained additional parameter or controller changes were introduced.
evidence: Before/after values, comparable run logs and a short explanation.
learning_phases.rollback: Restore the recorded original setting and repeat the baseline if needed.
learning_phases.teach_back: Did the requested speed equal the observed speed throughout the route, and why?
learning_phases.record: [Same-route speed comparison](../../evidence/l06-one-speed-change/README.md): only intentional setting WP_SPD10->1m/s, restored10 after landing/disarm. Peak measured speed3.120->0.990m/s and first identical low-speed near-goal sample3.258->5.782s. Same coordinate/frame/height; stock hover-learning/statistics updates retained and explained. Flight/cleanup and guided checkpoint complete on 2026-10-31. Learner identified acceleration, slowing and WP_SPD as a horizontal speed target. Follow-up clarified braking at the destination while holding height versus later landing/descent; guided understanding, not independent examination. One pair only; no controller tuning, firmware edits or new tests.

learning_phases.title: Measure stopping and arrival
learning_phases.goal: Distinguish passing a waypoint from reaching a low-speed held destination.
learning_phases.concept: Completion is a measured position, speed and dwell condition.
read_focus: Selected waypoint/hold behavior and relevant recorded telemetry.
Current proposed arrival thresholds, to be fixed for the scenario before qualification.
learning_phases.change_scope: Manual/log-based observation of stopping; no new controller or automatic test suite.
steps: Define the scenario's position, speed and dwell conditions before the run.
Observe deceleration, first entry into the region and continued hold.
Compare the waypoint-reached indicator with the full arrival contract.
success: Arrival/stop behavior is measured honestly, including drift, overshoot or failure.
The user can explain why a waypoint flag alone may be insufficient.
evidence: Position/speed/dwell timeline and the chosen scenario thresholds.
learning_phases.rollback: Return to the L05 configuration; retain the failed run and reason if arrival is not achieved.
learning_phases.teach_back: What evidence distinguishes a pass-through from a controlled stop?
learning_phases.record: [Measured entry, stopping and arrival](../../evidence/l07-measure-arrival/README.md): fixed1m/.3m/s/2s dwell plus height/state/freshness/gap conditions before stock L05-config run. First region entry2.418s at2.190m/s; first all-bounds sample3.164s; nine samples completed dwell at5.165s; further17.254s of qualifying sampled hold before LAND. About0.100m overshoot; no waypoint-reached message observed in selected GUIDED position path. Flight, landing/disarm, cleanup and guided checkpoint complete on 2026-10-31. Learner identified that first entry was too fast and one later low-speed sample was insufficient; continued held conditions were needed. Guided clarification fixed the timing, speed<=0.3m/s rather than exact zero, and two-second dwell terminology. Guided understanding, not independent examination. No parameter/controller changes or new tests.

learning_phases.title: Add a small native status slice
learning_phases.goal: Prove one bounded custom native component can build and report status while the stock flight mode remains active.
learning_phases.concept: Our native task logic belongs inside the maintained autopilot while reusing upstream flight facilities.
read_focus: Chosen revision's mode/module registration, build and scheduling conventions.
Native mission architecture and update-maintenance policy.
learning_phases.change_scope: One minimal native component/build/scheduling slice and bounded status output. Stock mode retains flight execution; custom mode activation/movement follows in L10.
steps: Select the smallest native component/status slice and list its necessary build/scheduling plumbing.
Add bounded status output while the qualified stock mode continues to own movement.
Build and manually verify the reported state and return to the untouched stock build.
success: The native status slice builds and reports actual status while stock mode retains flight execution.
Custom commits/diffs remain identifiable against the untouched baseline.
evidence: Scoped diff, build result, status output and scheduling/resource notes.
learning_phases.rollback: Revert the isolated custom slice or select the retained upstream build.
learning_phases.teach_back: Which part is our addition, and which stock behavior still owns movement?
learning_phases.record: [L08 evidence](../../evidence/l08-native-status-slice/README.md): isolated custom build passed; 13 native mode/arming status reports matched stock heartbeat while disarmed. Stock rollback observed for 78.04s without custom status; exact original hash preserved and owned sessions cleaned. Five-file diff/source pin, build output and scheduler-clock limitations retained. Guided learner checkpoint completed: learner identified the component as an observer whose removal loses only the added reports; clarification distinguished native C++ observation from GCS transport and retained stock mode/controller/mixer authority. This is guided understanding, not independent examination; user subsequently authorized feature-branch publication before L09; custom firmware commit 3f467d90be284654c5721ac3d94c26863f771275.

learning_phases.title: Admit one typed coordinate task
learning_phases.goal: Accept or reject a bounded coordinate-task definition in the native component without initiating movement.
learning_phases.concept: Data validation and authorization precede navigation.
read_focus: Proposed mission contract, actual ingress/receiver and native state model.
Frame/origin/reset, units, limits and required-input rules.
learning_phases.change_scope: One small typed task and its actual scoped ingress/status contract; no general language interpreter or movement.
steps: Choose/version the minimal coordinate task and identify its producer/receiver.
Implement bounded acceptance/rejection and explicit reasons for invalid frame, limits or prerequisites.
Manually submit a valid example and relevant invalid cases without starting flight execution.
success: Valid data is accepted and invalid/unsupported data is rejected with reasons.
Task admission cannot silently arm or start motion.
evidence: Exact schema/message mapping, submitted examples and native responses.
learning_phases.rollback: Disable/remove the scoped ingress change and retain the L08 status baseline.
learning_phases.teach_back: Why can a syntactically valid coordinate still be an invalid mission?
learning_phases.record: [L09 evidence](../../evidence/l09-native-task-contract/README.md): versioned USER_1 COMMAND_INT contract, bounded native admission and exact retained-home/task state. Final source manually produced22 status reports (one accepted, two duplicates,19 rejected); all later reports preserved task1. Includes fractional-version and sub-centimetre corrections with separate earlier evidence. All93 final-run heartbeats stayed disarmed/on-ground; original L08 rollback returned UNSUPPORTED and retained its hash. Scoped six-file diff, schema, commands, telemetry, source/binary identities and cleanup retained. Guided learner checkpoint complete: learner identified request validation/rejection and the receive/return flow without movement. Clarification distinguished task ID from coordinates, payload validity from home/navigation/vehicle readiness, and the already-wired/observed RAM admission from an unused function. Accepted data is stored; the switch maps its result to a MAVLink acknowledgment. This records guided understanding, not independent examination; User subsequently authorized L09 feature-branch publication before L10; firmware commit 39cf614d1aae2ee4acb93f9294ebf66178967acb. User-requested repository-style cleanup subsequently replaced positional Request/Context initialization with named field assignments; same bindings/policy, incremental build and diff check passed. Pre-cleanup manual evidence and current-source hashes are distinguished; no manual scenario rerun for this style-only change.

learning_phases.title: Execute one accepted native goal
learning_phases.goal: Use the native mode adapter to execute one already accepted coordinate task in a clear scene.
learning_phases.concept: Our coordinator selects the goal; reused navigation and controllers calculate movement.
read_focus: Qualified mode entry/exit and initialization from the selected revision.
Actual native call path into navigation/control; stock GUIDED messages are not assumed to feed this mode.
learning_phases.change_scope: One native known-goal execution path with vehicle/authority/navigation checks; reuse the L05 goal.
steps: Specify qualified entry/exit and the currently valid inputs before enabling movement.
Connect the accepted task to the selected existing navigation/control path.
Run the same known-goal scenario and compare its movement with the stock baseline.
success: The native owner executes the accepted goal and retains upstream authority/failsafe behavior.
Any difference from the stock baseline is explained and recorded.
evidence: Scoped integration diff, build pin, native state events and comparative trajectory.
learning_phases.rollback: Return to the retained stock build/mode and baseline scenario.
learning_phases.teach_back: Which part of the code changed the destination, and which generated motor demand?

learning_phases.title: Add native arrival and operator abort
learning_phases.goal: Report measured arrival and execute one qualified operator-abort path with clear native reasons.
learning_phases.concept: A task lifecycle is different from the lower-level controller loop.
read_focus: Native state transitions, L07 arrival observations and selected supported fallback.
Upstream arming, override and failsafe interaction.
learning_phases.change_scope: Small native arrival/dwell and operator-stop transitions; no arbitrary failure framework.
steps: Bind the measured arrival contract and bounded input-validity checks to the active task.
Implement one qualified operator-stop/abort transition with actual response reporting.
Manually demonstrate nominal arrival and an interrupted run.
success: Completion follows measured conditions, and abort shows actual state/reason.
Reconnect or duplicate requests do not restart or re-arm the task.
evidence: State transition timeline, nominal/abort logs and measured terminal behavior.
learning_phases.rollback: Revert the isolated lifecycle addition and use the last qualified configuration.
learning_phases.teach_back: Can a task be complete while the aircraft remains airborne, and what policy follows?

learning_phases.title: Connect one instrumented simulator scene
learning_phases.goal: Run the qualified flight baseline in one simple instrumented scene, preferably Gazebo.
learning_phases.concept: The scene/physics simulator and the SITL flight runtime have separate responsibilities.
read_focus: Official Gazebo plugin documentation and compatibility for the actual environment.
The selected world, vehicle plugin and sensor configuration.
learning_phases.change_scope: One compatible simulator/plugin/world integration; no AI, ROS by default or obstacle-avoidance changes.
steps: Select and record a compatible version tuple and native-Mac versus explicitly scoped fallback.
Launch one simple scene and verify the physics/sensor connection.
Repeat the existing baseline movement and document simulator differences.
success: The chosen scene and SITL exchange the intended outputs/measurements reproducibly.
No compatibility or collision evidence is claimed from a successful install alone.
evidence: Pinned simulator/plugin versions, launch files/commands and one baseline log.
learning_phases.rollback: Stop owned scene processes and return to basic SITL with the previous profile.
learning_phases.teach_back: Which program calculates flight control, and which simulates the world?

learning_phases.title: Observe one obstacle sensor
learning_phases.goal: See usable distance/proximity observations for one static obstacle before using them for control.
learning_phases.concept: A visible obstacle and a valid metric obstacle observation are different.
read_focus: Selected sensor geometry, mounting frame, range, timestamp and validity fields.
Actual observation transport and the downstream consumer.
learning_phases.change_scope: One simulated obstacle sensor and bounded observation path; no autonomous dodge behavior.
steps: Place one obstacle at known evaluation positions and configure one sensor.
Inspect observation direction, distance, timestamps, coverage and absence/invalid states.
Compare measurements with declared evaluation truth without feeding hidden truth into autonomy.
success: Sensor values and invalid/out-of-view behavior are understood and recorded.
Required clearance directions and coverage limits are explicit.
evidence: Sensor configuration, observation samples and comparison notes.
learning_phases.rollback: Disable the new sensor/integration and retain the baseline scene.
learning_phases.teach_back: Can a target bounding box establish the distance or clearance measured by this sensor?

learning_phases.title: Qualify one stock avoidance scenario
learning_phases.goal: Demonstrate one clear/blocked obstacle scenario using a documented supported stock mode and existing avoidance.
learning_phases.concept: Avoidance needs a destination, usable observations and a qualified mode/configuration.
read_focus: Selected stock avoidance behavior and its mode/input constraints.
AC_WPNav_OA/AP_OAPathPlanner or the actual chosen code path in the pinned source.
learning_phases.change_scope: One stock avoidance configuration and static scene; no custom planner or native-mode avoidance yet.
steps: Fix conservative motion/clearance criteria and the intended supported stock mode.
Run a clear route and a route with the single obstacle.
Observe the detour or bounded failure and inspect actual clearance/stop behavior.
success: The recorded stock path behaves as configured, with limitations retained.
A detected obstacle is not assumed to guarantee a globally feasible route.
evidence: Exact parameters, sensor profile, route/clearance observations and failures.
learning_phases.rollback: Restore baseline parameters and the clear scene.
learning_phases.teach_back: What additional inputs made avoidance work compared with a plain waypoint command?

learning_phases.title: Reuse avoidance in our native path
learning_phases.goal: Connect the qualified avoidance path to our native task and repeat the same scene.
learning_phases.concept: Custom modes do not automatically inherit stock AUTO/GUIDED behavior.
read_focus: Native adapter type/initialization and the selected avoidance handoff.
Planner processing/error/success and upstream mode/failsafe interaction.
learning_phases.change_scope: One explicit native avoidance integration and blocked-route policy; no general urban planner.
steps: Identify the exact shared navigation/avoidance objects and failure semantics.
Integrate the qualified path while preserving native task ownership and input validity.
Compare clear, single-obstacle and blocked behavior with L14.
success: Our mode uses the intended avoidance path and reports blocked/invalid outcomes honestly.
No infinite continuation on missing observations or unknown route viability is claimed.
evidence: Integration diff, scenario comparison, native reasons and actual trajectory.
learning_phases.rollback: Return to the last qualified native clear-scene build or the stock avoidance baseline.
learning_phases.teach_back: Which stock feature was reused, and which integration did we still need to write?

learning_phases.title: Show a minimal working operator preview
learning_phases.goal: Present a focused interactive React/MUI preview for one mission before application UI integration.
learning_phases.concept: A preview demonstrates controls and states; it does not prove vehicle execution.
read_focus: Control-console requirements and current native state/request contract.
The intended real React/MUI components and shared theme.
learning_phases.change_scope: One isolated working preview with labeled fixtures and disconnected callbacks; no live vehicle control.
steps: Build only connection/state, one coordinate mission, Start/Stop and event/result display.
Demonstrate pending, rejection, active, complete, stale and aborted states.
Show the working preview and record explicit approval of the shown scope before L17 integration.
success: The interactive preview is usable and its actual approval source/date/scope is recorded.
Static architecture images are not counted as UI approval.
evidence: Preview artifact/source and the actual shown-scope approval record when obtained.
learning_phases.rollback: Remove only task-owned preview processes/assets; retain needed component code and recorded review context.
learning_phases.teach_back: Which displayed states came from fixtures, and which would need firmware telemetry?

learning_phases.title: Connect the approved minimal console
learning_phases.additional_prerequisite: Explicit approval of the working L16 preview scope; new scope needs its own preview.
learning_phases.goal: Connect the approved controls to operator requests and firmware-reported state for one mission.
learning_phases.concept: The browser observes and requests; native code owns in-flight progression.
read_focus: Approved preview scope and the qualified native ingress/status contract.
External session/process ownership and stale/reconnect behavior.
learning_phases.change_scope: Only the approved console scope and smallest necessary external session adapter.
steps: Integrate the approved controls and bounded event/status display.
Exercise start/rejection/stop and reconnect against the qualified native mission.
Remove obsolete preview scaffolding and leave a clear start/stop entry point.
success: The UI reports actual native state and a reconnect cannot silently restart a mission.
Only owned processes are launched/cleaned and obsolete preview material is removed.
evidence: Approval reference, source diff, manual UI/mission observations and cleanup record.
learning_phases.rollback: Stop owned tooling and return to the existing console/qualified native baseline.
learning_phases.teach_back: What happens to an already accepted native mission when the browser closes?

learning_phases.title: Recognize one supported target without moving
learning_phases.goal: Qualify acquisition/identity for one chosen target class or reference in simulation.
learning_phases.concept: A detector finds image regions; supported targets and identity need evaluation.
read_focus: Selected detector/tracker classes, license/runtime and representative imagery.
Held-out scene/viewpoint evaluation and target-absence/identity-switch cases.
learning_phases.change_scope: One optional perception capability and its observations; no motion triggered by detections.
steps: Define one target/instance rule and representative labeled/negative scenes.
Evaluate an existing model first and adapt only if necessary.
Record acquisition failures, false detections, absence and identity continuity on held-out scenes.
success: The supported target claim matches retained evaluation evidence and limitations.
An unsupported class is reported explicitly rather than assumed recognized.
evidence: Model/profile/license references, dataset split rationale and actual outcomes.
learning_phases.rollback: Disable the optional worker; retain coordinate-only missions and preserve weights/data outside scope.
learning_phases.teach_back: What does this detector output, and what does it still not know about the object?

learning_phases.title: Estimate one object stopping goal without moving
learning_phases.goal: Produce a bounded metric stopping goal from target observations and a qualified range/pose source.
learning_phases.concept: Pixels, relative direction and a metric navigation destination are different representations.
read_focus: Camera/range calibration, capture-time pose, transforms, frames and uncertainty.
Object extent, vehicle extent and stopping-region construction.
learning_phases.change_scope: One geometry/goal producer and native input validation; no autonomous object approach yet.
steps: Verify range conventions and camera-to-body/navigation transforms.
Build a stopping region outside the target's occupied space and attach quality/time/uncertainty.
Compare goal error with evaluation truth across the bounded scenario.
success: Goal geometry and validity limits are measured and the native receiver rejects stale/invalid goals.
Hidden simulator object coordinates do not drive claimed sensor-based goals.
evidence: Calibration/profile, frame contract, goal observations and error results.
learning_phases.rollback: Disable the object-goal producer and retain the qualified coordinate task.
learning_phases.teach_back: Why is the center of a detection box not a safe destination in meters?

learning_phases.title: Approach one confirmed static object
learning_phases.goal: Use the accepted object stopping goal with the existing native approach/arrival machinery.
learning_phases.concept: Perception changes the goal source while qualified flight execution remains reusable.
read_focus: Goal-admission hysteresis/age policy and native active-step capability requirements.
The previously qualified route, clearance, stop and abort behavior.
learning_phases.change_scope: One object-dependent task step; no unbounded search or arbitrary landing.
steps: Enable the required target/geometry capability only for this task.
Approach a confirmed static target using the accepted stable goal.
Manually exercise absence/stale identity/large goal correction and retain the bounded outcome.
success: Measured arrival and clearance meet the fixed scenario contract, or the failure reason is retained.
Coordinate missions still run without an unused detector.
evidence: Native/perception timelines, arrival/clearance measurements and failed cases.
learning_phases.rollback: Select the retained coordinate mission and disable the optional perception path.
learning_phases.teach_back: Which part changed compared with the known-coordinate mission?

learning_phases.title: Search one bounded area
learning_phases.goal: Visit a small declared set of observation viewpoints and terminate with found/not-found.
learning_phases.concept: A target description supplies what to seek; a search region and policy supply where to look.
read_focus: Request-to-action notes, camera visibility and permitted route/viewpoint geometry.
Time/energy/geographic limits and preauthorized no-target policy.
learning_phases.change_scope: One bounded search policy using existing motion/perception; no language-driven exploration outside its limits.
steps: Fix a small search region/viewpoint set, visibility assumptions and termination rules.
Visit permitted viewpoints while recording actual coverage and confirmed candidates.
Demonstrate target absence and budget exhaustion without expanding the search silently.
success: The search ends within its declared bounds with explicit evidence/reason.
Occluded or unobserved space is not claimed searched.
evidence: Viewpoint/coverage record, budgets and found/not-found outcomes.
learning_phases.rollback: Disable the search step and return to one confirmed-target approach.
learning_phases.teach_back: How does the system choose where to go before it sees the target?

learning_phases.title: Assess one candidate landing patch
learning_phases.goal: Assess one bounded candidate ground patch without commanding a landing.
learning_phases.concept: Recognizing the nearby object does not establish landing-surface or descent suitability.
read_focus: Selected ground sensing/geometry, footprint, surface assumptions and descent corridor.
Validity/uncertainty and no-qualified-site policy.
learning_phases.change_scope: One observable landing-site assessment capability; no general arbitrary-terrain claim or descent control.
steps: Choose a simple declared surface and required footprint/clearance evidence.
Evaluate one acceptable and one unsuitable/unknown patch.
Publish a bounded candidate plus validity reasons for native acceptance/rejection.
success: The candidate claim matches measured surface/corridor evidence and rejected cases.
An unknown patch is not treated as acceptable merely because it is beside the target.
evidence: Surface/corridor observations, assessment limits and acceptance/rejection reasons.
learning_phases.rollback: Disable site assessment and retain the approach-and-hold task.
learning_phases.teach_back: What additional evidence is required for landing beyond locating the truck?

learning_phases.title: Land at one qualified simulated site
learning_phases.goal: Execute and verify landing at one admitted static simulated site using qualified ArduPilot behavior.
learning_phases.concept: A landing command, descent guidance and confirmed touchdown are separate conditions.
read_focus: Selected LAND/precision-landing path, mode handoff and required estimator/target inputs.
Site validity during descent and feasible interruption/terminal policy.
learning_phases.change_scope: One native landing handoff and touchdown verification for the admitted scenario.
steps: Qualify the selected landing path and native handoff in the simple site scenario.
Execute descent while checking required state/site observations.
Verify touchdown and terminal state; record the feasible outcome when the site/input becomes invalid.
success: Actual touchdown/terminal evidence is retained, with no arbitrary-site capability inferred.
Landing failure/interruption is distinguished from arrival or a paused simulator.
evidence: Site admission, mode/flight timeline and actual landing/failure outcomes.
learning_phases.rollback: Return to the qualified approach-and-hold scenario and previous mode/build.
learning_phases.teach_back: What measurement proves that landing completed?

learning_phases.title: Handle one link failure at a time
learning_phases.goal: Demonstrate distinct native outcomes for UI, ground and observation-producer link loss in separate runs.
learning_phases.concept: Different links have different owners and failure consequences.
read_focus: Native cached task policy, heartbeat ownership and selected failsafe configuration.
Required versus unused observation producers.
learning_phases.change_scope: One failure type per run and a narrowly scoped response/status change if required.
steps: Fix the expected policy for one link and retain a nominal baseline.
Disconnect that link in a bounded simulation and observe the actual response/reconnect behavior.
Repeat separately for the next relevant link; split code work if the response requires another independent behavior.
success: Each link failure is labeled correctly and no reconnect silently re-arms/restarts.
Observation-producer loss is not reported as merely a lost browser view.
evidence: Per-link configuration, event timelines and observed native/vehicle response.
learning_phases.rollback: Restore the connection/configuration and return to the retained nominal baseline.
learning_phases.teach_back: Why may losing the browser be different from losing the navigation/perception producer?

learning_phases.title: Qualify one alternative pose source with GPS available
learning_phases.goal: Observe and integrate one selected alternative pose source before relying on it for GPS-denied movement.
learning_phases.concept: A map or an IMU alone is not a qualified position estimate.
read_focus: Selected sensor/estimator assumptions, origin/frame/time alignment and quality/reset semantics.
ArduPilot external-navigation integration for the pinned build.
learning_phases.change_scope: One source/profile and observation/integration qualification; split sensor setup, alignment and fusion into additional cards if any becomes a separate unfamiliar change.
steps: Select one appropriate estimator/sensor source and define the alignment contract.
Observe its drift/quality while GPS remains available for baseline comparison.
Qualify its intended ArduPilot integration without claiming GPS-denied flight.
success: Alternative pose validity, frame alignment and limitations are measured.
Evaluation truth is not secretly used as the alternative sensor-only estimate.
evidence: Sensor/estimator/profile pin, alignment/quality results and observed reset/loss behavior.
learning_phases.rollback: Disable the alternative source configuration and retain the GPS baseline.
learning_phases.teach_back: What produces the alternative position estimate before ArduPilot can use it?

learning_phases.title: Fly one known goal with GPS unavailable
learning_phases.goal: Run the bounded known-goal mission using the qualified alternative navigation source.
learning_phases.concept: Losing GPS differs from losing all usable localization.
read_focus: Qualified source selection/transition and navigation-health policy.
Known-goal behavior and actual feasible fallback when position validity is lost.
learning_phases.change_scope: One GPS-unavailable-from-start scenario; GPS loss during flight follows as a separate run/change.
steps: Fix the navigation inputs and verify there is no hidden ground-truth control path.
Repeat the known-goal mission with GPS unavailable from the start.
Separately examine in-flight GPS loss only after the baseline works.
success: Actual trajectory error and terminal behavior are retained with explicit sensing provenance.
Invalid localization produces the qualified feasible response rather than assumed Hold/RTL.
evidence: Input provenance, source configuration, trajectory error and failure outcomes.
learning_phases.rollback: Restore the qualified GPS profile and nominal scenario.
learning_phases.teach_back: Why does turning off GPS not automatically mean the vehicle can still hold position?

learning_phases.title: Repeat the qualified scenarios then combine failures
learning_phases.goal: Run a fixed evidence campaign for only the capabilities actually qualified.
learning_phases.concept: One successful run is not repeatability or a general reliability claim.
read_focus: Actual accepted scenario/phase evidence, fixed thresholds and version/configuration pins.
Capability-specific P08 campaign and failure metrics.
learning_phases.change_scope: Manual/existing-check campaign; no new automated tests, snapshots or test scaffolding.
steps: Predeclare nominal and individual-fault scenarios and their counts before tuning.
Retain all outcomes and compare against fixed criteria.
Combine faults only after each relevant capability passes; include object/search/landing cases only when their own prerequisites passed.
success: Reported counts include failures, exclusions and unsupported cases.
Phase/milestone completion reflects actual evidence rather than an optimistic aggregate.
evidence: Scenario manifest, all run outcomes, versions and accepted limits.
learning_phases.rollback: Retain the last qualified version/configuration and fix one failed capability at a time.
learning_phases.teach_back: What claim does this campaign support, and what remains unproven?

learning_phases.title: Review the separate SkyDive prototype
learning_phases.goal: Document reusable screen/input behavior and its limits without changing the prototype.
learning_phases.concept: A visual game demonstration and an instrumented ArduPilot flight are different evidence paths.
read_focus: Existing prototype recordings/configuration and the unresolved contact report.
Capture, region tracking, HUD decoding and key scheduling responsibilities.
learning_phases.change_scope: Read-only review and a scoped reuse note; no changes to the preserved prototype.
steps: Inspect the existing source/evidence within scope.
Identify reusable pieces and distinguish tracking from semantic detection.
Record the interface limits and proposed separate integration.
success: Existing evidence is labeled honestly and prototype/private files remain preserved.
evidence: Reuse map, actual evidence references and limitations.
learning_phases.rollback: No prototype modifications to revert; preserve the reviewed originals.
learning_phases.teach_back: Which claims can this visual demonstration support, and which need instrumented SITL evidence?

learning_phases.title: Integrate the separate approved SkyDive demonstration
learning_phases.additional_prerequisite: Any added SkyDive UI scope requires its own working preview approval.
learning_phases.goal: Qualify one selected-region visual approach through the separate game adapter.
learning_phases.concept: Screen/input control has different Stop and arrival semantics from ArduPilot.
read_focus: Approved backend/target-selection UI scope and prototype reuse note.
Focus/permissions/input handling and visual review criteria.
learning_phases.change_scope: One separate backend/scene/command profile; split UI additions behind the existing preview gate.
steps: Show/approve any added interactive UI scope before integration.
Integrate only scoped reusable adapter pieces and one scene/profile.
Perform the fixed continuous-approach review and retain all outcomes and cleanup.
success: The proposed repeatability gate is actually observed or its limitation/failure retained.
No metric arrival or ArduPilot bridge is inferred from visual closeness.
evidence: Shown-scope approval, recordings, configuration and actual visual review.
learning_phases.rollback: Stop owned tooling, release inputs and preserve the original prototype/configuration.
learning_phases.teach_back: Why is a paused game not the same as a landed or hovering aircraft?

learning_phases.title: Define a separate hardware qualification program
learning_phases.goal: Document a scoped hardware program before selecting any physical implementation work.
learning_phases.concept: Simulation evidence does not qualify a real vehicle or authorize operation.
read_focus: Qualified simulation subset and actual hardware/resource/sensor requirements.
Separate physical-deployment and operating-context requirements.
learning_phases.change_scope: Planning only until separately scoped authorization; no purchase, provisioning or physical operation.
steps: Choose the relevant proven simulation subset and identify transfer gaps.
Draft the hardware/process deployment and qualification sequence.
Keep procurement/physical work subject to its separately authorized scope.
success: The proposed hardware scope, limits, resources and qualification plan are concrete and reviewable.
evidence: Separate proposed hardware/deployment/qualification document and actual decisions.
learning_phases.rollback: Retain the simulation baseline; no physical state is changed by this planning card.
learning_phases.teach_back: Which simulation assumptions need new evidence on actual hardware?
